author: shared
title: Data Structures: Lists and Tuples
notes: Split from examples/comp101_w5_w6.owl by taughtIn=W5_lists. Interim README layout before full merge/test.

entity_types.name: Lecture
entity_types.definition: A week or unit in the course schedule.

entity_types.name: DataType
entity_types.definition: A Python built-in type used in code (e.g. list, dict).

entity_types.name: Pattern
entity_types.definition: A common loop or problem-solving pattern (e.g. Accumulator).

entity_types.name: Invokable
entity_types.definition: Callable Python API: type-bound methods and global built-in functions.

entity_types.name: ConceptCarrier
entity_types.definition: Python surface that can implement or use curriculum concepts (syntax, methods, builtins). Groups LanguageConstruct with invokables for T-box connectivity.

entity_types.name: Method
entity_types.definition: A function bound to a data type (e.g. list.append()).

entity_types.name: Concept
entity_types.definition: An idea to understand, not a keyword (e.g. Indexing).

entity_types.name: Skill
entity_types.definition: A learning outcome the student should achieve.

entity_types.name: BuiltInFunction
entity_types.definition: A global built-in function such as len() or sorted() (adopted from the shared OOP T-Box; cleaner than modelling these as LanguageConstructs).

entity_types.name: ErrorType
entity_types.definition: An exception students may encounter (e.g. IndexError).

entity_types.name: LanguageConstruct
entity_types.definition: Python syntax such as a for loop or the [] operator.

relations.name: hasMethod
relations.definition: Inverse of methodOf: a type or class has this method.

relations.name: requiredBy
relations.definition: Inverse of requiresConcept: this concept is required by the given skill.

relations.name: throwsError
relations.definition: An operation/construct can raise this error type. Prefer Method, BuiltInFunction, or LanguageConstruct carriers — not bare DataType nodes.

relations.name: dependsOn
relations.definition: Strict prerequisite: the source should be learned after the target. Transitive, so prerequisite chains close automatically (adopted from the OOP T-Box).

relations.name: isProducedBy
relations.definition: Inverse of producesType: this data type is produced by the given method or built-in function.

relations.name: precedes
relations.definition: Inverse of recommendedBefore: the source normally comes later in the teaching sequence.

relations.name: revisits
relations.definition: Inverse of revisitedIn: a lecture reinforces this entity from an earlier week.

relations.name: raisedBy
relations.definition: Inverse of throwsError: this error is raised by the given entity.

relations.name: implementsConcept
relations.definition: Syntax-level coding of a concept (LanguageConstruct). BuiltInFunctions use usesConcept instead — do not attach implementsConcept to builtins.

relations.name: methodOf
relations.definition: A method belongs to a type or class. Range widened to owl:Thing to also cover user-defined classes in the OOP module.

relations.name: revisitedIn
relations.definition: Week where a concept introduced earlier is reinforced in a new context — not first taught here.

relations.name: enables
relations.definition: Inverse of dependsOn: the source is a prerequisite that enables the target.

relations.name: usesConcept
relations.definition: A method, construct, or built-in function relies on / carries out a concept or abstract operation (create, access, remove, ...). Shared name with the OOP module (replaces the earlier performsOperation).

relations.name: producesType
relations.definition: The data type a method or built-in function returns (adopted from the OOP module; richer than the returnsNone boolean, which is kept as a shortcut).

relations.name: isUsedBy
relations.definition: Inverse of usesConcept: this concept/operation is used by the given method, construct, or built-in function.

relations.name: implementedBy
relations.definition: Inverse of implementsConcept: a concept is coded by this language construct, method, or built-in.

relations.name: recommendedBefore
relations.definition: Soft order among sibling peers when PATH / dependsOn do not already decide which to introduce first (a teaching dilemma). NOT the tutor spine — that total order is only in comp101_path_w5_w6.json (/path/next). Do not sprinkle on every consecutive PATH pair; skip when traversal order is already determined. Distinct from dependsOn (strict readiness) and confusedWith (student mix-ups).

relations.name: teaches
relations.definition: Inverse of taughtIn: a lecture first introduces this entity.

relations.name: confusedWith
relations.definition: Two entities students often confuse and should explicitly distinguish (e.g. list vs tuple, set.discard vs set.remove). Symmetric. COMP101-specific name: OOP keeps contrastsWith for opposites/alternatives/confused concepts (Concept↔Concept).

relations.name: requiresConcept
relations.definition: A skill requires understanding of a concept.

relations.name: taughtIn
relations.definition: Week where an entity is first introduced (primary teaching). Use revisitedIn for reinforcement in a later week.
